reviewer.independence: Did not implement commit 4273c3d9, did not edit shipping source, and only added held-out evidence plus this follow-up review record in the detached checker worktree.

comparator.notes: Strict SVG comparison against Java goldens using the provided prebuilt helper. No Cargo or rustc commands were run in this checker pass.

java: CommandLinkClass resolves both relationship endpoints through CucaDiagram#quarkInContextSafe(true, entString) and only creates a leaf when quark.getData() is null.

CucaDiagram#quarkInContextSafe preserves the exact supplied endpoint string. With separators enabled it returns root.child(full) or currentQuark.child(full); with a null separator it firstWithName(full) matches the raw name, never an identifier-normalized surrogate.
For group endpoints, Bibliotekon#getNodeUid returns Cluster.getSpecialPointId(ent), and ClusterDotString emits that point when a link touches the group.
rust: 4273c3d9 adds resolve_quoted_relationship_endpoint, which probes the raw quoted endpoint against existing entity/package quark paths, then falls back to resolve_relationship_endpoint(strip_creole_for_id(raw)).

That fallback is already non-Java for genuinely missing quoted class endpoints: Java would create a new leaf named from the raw quoted text, while Rust normalizes whitespace and markup into an identifier-shaped name before creation.

The same fallback can also misbind to an unrelated existing normalized class (for example Quoted_Missing_9021) instead of creating a fresh raw-name leaf when the quoted display collides with an existing normalized identifier.
source_inspection.runtime_note: Using the provided prebuilt no-oracle helper for revision 4273c3d9, the shipped path still emits normalized synthetic classes on fresh quoted cases, including a reopened bare quoted-package target that Java routes directly to the existing cluster.
source_inspection.fixture_shaping_search: No mechanism-name string, prior held-out filename, or similar fixture-shaped branch was found in shipping crates.
source_inspection.constants: No new mechanism-shaped constants were introduced by 4273c3d9; the implementation diff is parser-only.

perturbations.evidence: Java creates a new class with data-qualified-name and link id text "Quoted Missing 9001". Rust creates Quoted_Missing_9001 instead, widening the root SVG to 205px and changing both entity text and relationship metadata.

Java renders a target class named "Quoted Missing 9012" and link id="Source9011-to-Quoted Missing 9012". Rust again normalizes the target to Quoted_Missing_9012, changing both the label text and SVG metadata.

Java keeps the declared class Quoted_Missing_9021 and also creates a second class "Quoted Missing 9021" for the quoted endpoint. Rust reuses the existing normalized class and never creates the raw quoted leaf, collapsing the diagram from 27 elements to 20.

axes: quoted display name versus explicit alias
perturbations.evidence: Java treats the display-only reference "Quoted Alias 9031" as a new class and links it to Sink9032. Rust instead synthesizes Quoted_Alias_9031, proving the normalized fallback also mis-models quoted display versus aliased identity.

Java links Source9043 directly to the existing cluster Quoted Reopen 9041 (data-entity-2="ent0002", link id="Source9043-to-Quoted Reopen 9041"). The provided 4273c3d9 no-oracle helper instead synthesizes a class Quoted_Reopen_9041 (ent0005) and routes the edge to that class.

findings: REJECT: the account's planned normalized fallback for genuinely missing quoted class endpoints is not PlantUML's model. Java preserves the raw quoted endpoint text when it has to create a missing leaf.

REJECT: the normalized fallback can also bind to an unrelated existing normalized class instead of creating the fresh raw quoted leaf that Java creates, as shown by followup2_quoted_missing_collision_tb.

REJECT: end-to-end no-oracle behavior at the provided 4273c3d9 helper still fails a reopened bare quoted-package target, synthesizing Quoted_Reopen_9041 instead of routing to the existing filled group cluster.
No fixture-shaped shipping logic or new unexplained mechanism constants were found; the failures come from identity/path behavior, not from obvious overfitting.
